answer:
The Song dynasty was succeeded by the **Yuan dynasty** (the Mongol dynasty), which ruled China from approximately 1279 to 1368.

The last emperor of the Yuan dynasty was **Toghon Temür** (r. 1333–1368). Also known as Emperor Huizong of Yuan, he held this position for 35 years, making him one of the longest-reigning Yuan emperors after Kublai Khan. His reign marked the final period of Mongol rule in China and ended with his abdication in 1368, following which the Ming dynasty was established, bringing the Yuan dynasty to an end.
